person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: The connectivity distribution of large real networks - film-actor collaboration, the world wide web, the western US power grid and scientific citation - and what generates it.
span.quote: Exploring several large databases describing the topology of large networks that span as diverse fields as the www or the citation patterns in science

span.label: Why does the connectivity of large real networks follow a power law, when the established random-graph models predict that highly connected vertices should be practically absent?
span.quote: A common feature of the ER and WS models is that the probability of finding a highly connected vertex (that is, a large k) decreases exponentially with k, thus vertices with large connectivity are practically absent.

span.label: Identifies growth and preferential attachment as the two mechanisms that generate scale-free connectivity, and gives a model reproducing it.
span.quote: While these and other system-specific features could modify the exponent γ, our model offers the first successful mechanism accounting for the scale-invariant nature of real networks.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: This feature is found to be a consequence of the two generic mechanisms that networks expand continuously by the addition of new vertices, and new vertices attach preferentially to already well connected sites.

span.label: scale-free degree distribution in large networks
span.quote: A common property of many large networks is that the vertex connectivities follow a scale-free power-law distribution.

span.label: simulation
span.quote: To verify that both ingredients are necessary, we investigated two variants of the model.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: network growth with preferential attachment (new nodes attach preferentially to already-highly-connected nodes; a rich-gets-richer process) generates the scale-free power law
span.quote: incorporate growth and preferential attachment

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: growth - the network is open and gains vertices continuously, so N is not fixed
span.quote: In contrast, most real world networks are open, they form by the continuous addition of new vertices to the system, thus the number of vertices, N, increases throughout the lifetime of the network.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: preferential attachment - a new vertex attaches with probability proportional to a vertex's existing connectivity
span.quote: These examples indicate that the probability with which a new vertex connects to the existing vertices is not uniform, but there is a higher probability to be linked to a vertex that already has a large number of connections.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: compounding: an early advantage in connectivity widens as the network grows, so old vertices become hubs
span.quote: Due to the preferential attachment, a vertex that acquired more connections than another one will increase its connectivity at a higher rate, thus an initial difference in the connectivity between two vertices will increase further as the network grows.

span.label: the model reproduces the scale-free degree distribution but cannot account for all aspects of real networks
span.note: what this limits: every application of the model beyond the degree distribution: IT CANNOT BE EXPECTED TO ACCOUNT FOR ALL ASPECTS OF THE STUDIED NETWORKS
span.quote: While it reproduces the observed scale-free distribution, the proposed model cannot be expected to account for all aspects of the studied networks.

span.label: The model is not expected to capture everything about the networks it is fitted to.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0
span.quote: While it reproduces the observed scale-free distribution, the proposed model cannot be expected to account for all aspects of the studied networks.

span.label: Only a few real networks have detailed topological data available to test against.
span.note: what this limits: the empirical support for the whole claim: DETAILED TOPOLOGICAL DATA IS AVAILABLE ONLY FOR A FEW of the systems that form complex networks
span.quote: While there are a large number of systems that form complex networks, detailed topological data is available only for a few.

span.label: The model assumes strictly linear preferential attachment.
span.note: what this limits: every result derived from the model: IN THE MODEL WE ASSUMED LINEAR PREFERENTIAL ATTACHMENT - an assumption, not a measurement
span.quote: For example, in the model we assumed linear preferential attachment, that is

span.label: The single model exponent does not match the spread of exponents measured across the real networks.
span.note: what this limits: the predicted exponent specifically: THE EXPONENTS OBTAINED FOR THE DIFFERENT NETWORKS ARE SCATTERED BETWEEN 2.1 AND 4, while the model gives a single value
span.quote: Furthermore, the exponents obtained for the different networks are scattered between 2.1 and 4.

span.label: The model is not offered as a full account of the systems it is fitted to.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0
span.quote: While it reproduces the observed scale-free distribution, the proposed model cannot be expected to account for all aspects of the studied networks.

span.label: Attachment is assumed linear; scaling survives only at that exponent, which is a strong assumption rather than a result.
span.note: what this limits: the scale-free result itself, which survives at one parameter value only: SIMULATIONS INDICATE THAT SCALING IS PRESENT ONLY FOR alpha = 1
span.quote: simulations indicate that scaling is present only for α = 1

span.label: The model gives γ = 3 while the measured exponents run from 2.1 to 4, so the central prediction does not match any of the four datasets exactly.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 4 - the central prediction against the measured spread
span.quote: the exponents obtained for the different networks are scattered between 2.1 and 4

span.label: The paper's dynamic prediction about how a vertex accumulates edges over time could not be tested with the data available.
span.note: what this limits: the dynamic growth prediction, which is untested here: A SCALING PROPERTY THAT COULD BE DIRECTLY TESTED ONCE TIME-RESOLVED DATA ON NETWORK CONNECTIVITY BECOMES AVAILABLE
span.quote: a scaling property that could be directly tested once time-resolved data on network connectivity becomes available

span.label: The power-law region for the power grid is weak, and the paper says so rather than fitting it anyway.
span.note: what this limits: the power-grid case only: DUE TO THE RELATIVELY MODEST SIZE OF THE NETWORK, CONTAINING ONLY 4941 VERTICES, THE SCALING REGION IS LESS PROMINENT
